subject: Request: chronological access timeline / audit export format
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Chen <diane.chen@pioneerbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & export options for access audit (post-demo)

Hi Diane —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Pioneer asked for an export of "who accessed what and when" for the last 90 days to satisfy an internal audit.
- You mentioned CSV or parquet would be OK, and the security team prefers a chronological timeline view (events sorted by timestamp).
- Open question: do you need principal names, roles, IP addresses, and API key IDs in the export, or is an obfuscated principal ID sufficient?

Attached is a short note that outlines the fields Redwood can include by default and options for PII minimization. If you prefer, we can produce two flavors: (1) full-detail CSV, (2) redacted CSV with obfuscated principals and IPs.

Next steps from us:
1) I will put together a sample CSV export showing the column layout and timestamp granularity (we can do millisecond or second resolution).
2) Please confirm required fields (principal email vs principal ID, include IP, include agent string).
3) Let us know if you need a signed evidence pack (PDF with signed manifest) or simply the raw export.

Can you confirm the data retention window Pioneer wants included (90 days as discussed?), and whether the export should include failed access attempts and system/service accounts?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if handy.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0127

Attachment: redwood_audit_note.txt (summary of fields & redaction options)

From: Diane Chen <diane.chen@pioneerbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pioneer Bank Security <security@pioneerbank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up & export options for access audit (post-demo)

Markus —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side (security team inline):

- Confirm retention window: yes, 90 days. Also a separate export for 7-day high-frequency events would be useful for an ongoing incident review.
- Required fields: principal email OR hashed principal ID (either is fine). We prefer hashed principal IDs for the external export.
- IP addresses: include them but mask the last octet (e.g., 10.11.12.xxx) unless the request is coming from internal audit (then we can accept full IP).
- We need an event type column (read/write/admin), resource path, timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), request_id, and service component.
- Failed access attempts: include them, but mark as failed=true.
- Ordering: chronological ascending is preferred (oldest first).

Also: is it possible to get a separate small sample (first 500 rows) in CSV and a schema mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood fields to our SOC audit taxonomy? That helps our auditors validate quickly.

Thank you,
Diane Chen
Sr. Manager, Information Security
Pioneer Bank
security@pioneerbank.com

On a related note, our procurement team will ask for an evidence manifest (signed hash) if we accept the export into their compliance repository.

—
Pioneer Bank Security Team (cc'd)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Chen <diane.chen@pioneerbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & export options for access audit (post-demo)

Diane —

Thanks — this is very helpful. We'll produce two artifacts:

A) sample_access_export.csv (first 500 rows) with masked IPs and hashed principal IDs; chronological ascending; includes failed=true where relevant.
B) audit_mapping_key.xlsx that maps columns to Pioneer SOC taxonomy and indicates redaction decisions.

A couple of technical notes:
- Timestamp precision will be ISO 8601 in UTC to avoid TZ issues.
- We can include agent strings but can redact them if Pioneer considers them sensitive.
- We will attach a signed manifest (SHA256 of CSV) in a simple PDF for procurement.

Proposed delivery: Monday, 2026-08-31 by 11:00 PT — does that work for your audit team? If you need it earlier, we can expedite.

Action items:
- Diane: confirm whether procurement requires a notarized signature or a signed PDF manifest is sufficient.
- Rishi: can you build the export with masked IP and hashed principal id? Rishi, I put a short checklist in the attached note.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: audit_mapping_key.xlsx (column -> SOC mapping)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Chen <diane.chen@pioneerbank.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & export options for access audit (post-demo)

Diane / team —

Attached is the sample CSV (500 rows) and the mapping key per your specs. A couple implementation notes inline:

- principal_id: SHA256 of email lowercased (salted per Pioneer request). We will share salt via secure channel if you want to rehash.
- ip_address: last octet masked (xxx). If you authorize full IP, we can deliver a version for internal audit only.
- event_timestamp: UTC, ISO-8601, second precision.
- request_id and component fields are guaranteed unique and mapped to our internal trace id.

Files attached: sample_access_export.csv (CSV stub — first 5 rows shown for preview), audit_mapping_key.xlsx, redwood_audit_note.txt (manifest and SHA256: abc123def456... )

If the format is good, we'll schedule a secure SFTP drop and share the signed manifest PDF via DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment: sample_access_export.csv (CSV preview), redwood_audit_note.txt (manifest)
